name: Manuscript preparation and publication
one_line: One manuscript carried through one venue's review lifecycle: drafts and their version family, the submission packet, editorial correspondence, referee reports, the response to reviewers, proofs and the licence that closes it.

node_test.why: The Research schema's default situation is research.project-workspace, whose recommended order is 00's own "a Research template may define project → stage → artifact type". This node differs on all three of the node test's axes. Detection: the signals here are submission-lifecycle ones that do not fire on workspace material at all — a venue-issued manuscript-id token, a cover letter addressed to an editor, an editorial-office reply chain, a referee report, a typeset proof with author queries, a submission archive manifest. Dimensions: venue enters the recommended order, which the schema row deliberately excluded, its own template note reserving venue and lab for situations that are separate template rows on this schema. Privacy: an unpublished manuscript under embargo and a confidential referee report are not the same review surface as a project's working figures, and the editorial correspondence arrives as mail, which 00 requires be handled "while treating addresses and message content as potentially sensitive". No child node is proposed for any lifecycle step: cover letter, referee report, response to reviewers and proof are VALUES of artifact_type, and the workflow position is a value of stage.

fields_note: A template references its schema's fields and never copies them. The five keys this situation actually uses are the Research schema's own: project, venue and stage as the recommended dimensions, artifact_type as the leaf fact that is deliberately flattened out of the order, and lab as a legal-but-metadata fact. authored_by is used here only as the discriminator that separates the holder's own manuscript from a downloaded paper, and 00 forbids it as a folder level: "It should avoid using authorship or creator identity as a destination dimension."

proposed_fields.example: the tracking token an editorial system issues for one submission and repeats in the subject line, the proof header and the portal page
proposed_fields.why_no_existing_key_works: This situation's strongest join handle is the submission tracking token, and no canonical key holds it. `project` is the research project and one project produces many submissions; `venue` is the journal and one venue receives many of the holder's manuscripts; `version_family` is the universal draft-family fact, computed from content and stem, whereas this token is an observed labelled value that spans several version families (the original and the revision are the same submission under different stems). Without a key to hold it, the evidence that actually ties the editorial email, the proof, the portal capture and the response document together has no shared validated fact to be shared, so the tie can only be expressed as retrieval similarity — which 00 says is never enough on its own. Recorded because 00's rule is that fields are the stable vocabulary: "The system may create new values when it sees a new course, project, company, university, or event, but it should not invent new fields automatically."
proposed_fields.not_authored_here: This node does not write the key into canonical_fields.json and does not put it in dimension_order — a template may only branch on fields its schema declares, and a folder level per submission id would be exactly the split 00 warns the canvas about: a level that "creates a large number of tiny folders". If R1c or Joseph adopts it, it belongs on the Research schema as a search and grouping field with destination_eligible false. Until then this node recommends nothing that depends on it, and the recognition signals below treat a manuscript-id-shaped token as evidence, never as a fact.

deterministic: a submission-lifecycle term (cover letter, response to reviewers, revision, referee report, proof, camera-ready) co-occurring with venue evidence or a manuscript-id-shaped token in a filename, title, page-one heading or an email subject zone — the pattern-plus-context shape, not the term alone

an editorial-office message: a subject carrying a manuscript-id-shaped token beside a decision word, from a sender at a venue-shaped domain, read from the fields 00 requires the mail extractor to yield — "sender, recipients, subject, sent date, thread identifiers, message body, attachment names, and reply-chain context"

an archive manifest whose members combine a manuscript, a cover letter, a figure sequence and supplementary material, read without unpacking — 00: "the normal scan should never extract archive contents to the filesystem", and the manifest is what the archive extractor stores: "the archive type, contained paths, filenames, folder names, extensions, file count, uncompressed size where available, and recognizable markers such as source-code manifests or document names"

a venue gazetteer hit matched at a word boundary in a filename, title, page-one heading or a cover-letter salutation, and not a hit whose only occurrence is in the reference-list zone — 00: "A course code or university name found in a filename, title, or page-one heading is more meaningful than the same text appearing once in a reference list on page eighteen"
a proof structure: a publisher-branded typeset layout carrying numbered author-query boxes and an article-id running header, which no working draft has
a version-family signal over one manuscript stem (00's "duplicate and version-family signals") — this establishes the family and the review surface, and it never establishes stage

a labelled slot in a structured source naming the manuscript title, the corresponding author or the submission date — a form field on a licence agreement or a portal export cell — which is 00's "labeled form field" direct-fact path
needs_llm: whether a draft is pre-submission working material (the project-workspace situation) or a submitted version, when no lifecycle term, venue or manuscript-id evidence fires anywhere in the file

stage read from unlabelled prose — a sentence saying the reviewers' comments have been addressed, or that this is the version for typesetting — which is the interpretation 00 assigns the model: "interpret an unusual research artifact"
whether a journal-formatted PDF is the holder's own output or somebody else's reading material, when the author list is only recoverable through OCR
whether a heterogeneous archive is one venue's submission packet or an unrelated download bundle

whether an OCR'd capture is a submission portal status page, a proof page, or an unrelated screen — 00 lists the alternatives an opaque image holds: it "may be a screenshot of a receipt, application portal, conversation, code error, or research figure"
never_alone: a venue or journal name alone. The tempting false file is the downloaded paper Ravikumar_2019_NatureMethods.pdf: it carries a masthead, a DOI and a journal name in high-weight zones and is reading material, for which 00 names a residual home — "papers, articles, reports, and saved PDFs that appear to be reading material but have no active research, course, or project association". The role question is 00's own: "Columbia can appear as an authoring school, course provider, target institution, employer, research venue, or merely a cited organization"
a DOI or a citation string alone

a finality or version token alone as stage — final, FINAL, v7, REV2, camera-ready in a filename are version-family evidence, and 00 warns off exactly these numbers: "numbers that look like years but are course identifiers, version numbers, build numbers, ZIP codes, or other unrelated values"
a bare four-digit number alone as a year, an article number or a manuscript id
a source_type alone: archive, email, image, ocr and text_document all appear here and none of them proves this situation; the extension is a routing signal
the absence of camera EXIF alone as proof that a portal capture is a screenshot — 00: "the system must not mistake the absence of EXIF for proof that an image is a screenshot"
a filename alone on an unreadable or password-protected submission archive — 00: "the system should not infer a purpose from their filename alone"

work_types_note: These are VALUES of the Research schema's artifact_type field, discovered at runtime. None is a roster node and none licenses a child template. The workflow position each implies (submitted, under review, revision, accepted, in proof) is likewise a value of stage.
grouping_reasons: one manuscript's version family across its drafts, the submitted version, the revision and the proof — the universal version-family fact is the anchor, and 00 keeps identity on the bytes, not the name: "If a file retains its name but its content hash changes, the system treats it as a new version"
one submission to one venue: the packet's archive members, the cover letter, the decision message, the referee reports and the response document, tied by a repeated manuscript-id-shaped token
one manuscript across successive venues after a rejection — the same project and the same version family, two venue-scoped submission neighbourhoods
one manuscript's figure set: panel files that repeat inside the manuscript and the submission manifest
00's own label for this neighbourhood is a research one, not a venue one: "PVA/RDP — Manuscripts and Figures"

a sparse lifecycle file (a response document or a figure panel with no project token) joins the neighbourhood as a context-supported member and acquires no project fact — 00: "The graph does not automatically copy those missing facts onto sparse files."

template.why: A recommendation for one organizational situation, not a filesystem: "The system recommends an order based on the domain template, but the user can reverse, remove, add, or flatten dimensions." project stays first for 00's stated reason — "For document and record domains, project, function, or subject usually comes before time because putting year first scatters related work across calendar folders" — and because it is the fact that survives a rejection and a resubmission. venue is the level this template adds and the schema's default order deliberately leaves out: a manuscript that goes to one journal, is rejected, and goes to another produces two complete submission families whose stage values repeat, so putting stage above venue interleaves two submissions under one Revision folder. It is also the parent-makes-the-child-intelligible rule applied to this material — 00 states it as "A work type such as Homework 3 is meaningful only after the course is known", and a file named Response to Reviewers is meaningless until the reader knows whose reviewers. stage is the leaf because it is the axis the user actually navigates while the work is live. artifact_type is a legal fact and is deliberately NOT a fourth level: at the stage leaf most branches would hold a handful of files and 00 asks the canvas to warn when a level "produces only one child, repeats a concept already expressed in the parent, creates excessive depth, or creates a large number of tiny folders". The same warning is the honest caveat on venue itself: a manuscript that only ever went to one journal makes venue a one-child level, and flattening it is the expected user edit, which the canvas can show before the user commits because it reports the branch counts each split would create. lab is legal here and is metadata only — a manuscript's producing lab is constant across the whole branch, so a level on it would repeat the parent.

collides_with.signal: The same project token, the same manuscript stem and the same drafts support both, so project, artifact_type and version_family evidence discriminates neither. The discriminating evidence is submission-lifecycle evidence about the file itself: a salutation addressed to an editor, a venue-issued manuscript-id token, a referee report, an author-query proof structure, or a submission manifest. A pre-submission draft carrying none of those is workspace material and this template must not take the item. Fixture: PVA-RDP_manuscript_v7_JR-comments.docx sits on the workspace side until a venue or a lifecycle term appears.

Both situations are venue-scoped, so a venue gazetteer hit and an abstract structure support both. The discriminating evidence is which lifecycle the file belongs to: peer-review correspondence (referee reports, a response document, proofs, a licence agreement) is this template; a presentation artifact (poster, slide deck, abstract-book entry, registration record) is the conference one, which the roster also gives ownership of the presentation source_type. A conference paper that then goes through journal review is two situations on one project, not one item counting twice.

A journal masthead, a DOI, a venue name and an academic paper structure support both sides identically — this is the tempting false file for this template. The discriminating evidence is authorship plus lifecycle: the holder's own manuscript carries a manuscript-id token, a submission packet, an editorial thread or an author-query proof; a collected paper carries a DOI and an author list without the holder and no lifecycle evidence at all. Absent lifecycle evidence the reading side is the better-supported one. Fixture: Ravikumar_2019_NatureMethods.pdf.

A thesis chapter and a journal manuscript are often the same text, so project, stage, artifact_type and a heavy version family support both. The discriminating evidence is which body is reviewing it: a committee, a defense schedule, a degree programme's formatting or submission rules put the file on the thesis side; an editorial office, a venue, referee reports and proofs put it here. A chapter that is also a submitted paper legitimately holds both situations on disjoint evidence.

A term paper or lab report written in journal form carries the same Abstract, Methods, Results and Discussion structure a manuscript carries, and both talk about results and figures. The discriminating evidence is which pattern the item sits beside: a course-code pattern with academic context (00's five terms) puts the file on coursework, while a venue or manuscript-id token with submission-lifecycle evidence puts it here. A student paper that names a journal in its bibliography is not a submission.

A LaTeX or notebook manuscript source sitting inside a version-controlled directory supports both, because a manuscript source IS source text. The discriminator is the one 00 states: "Code-related files should rely heavily on local structural evidence, including repository roots and package files" — a repository root or package manifest above the file counts for the code side; a journal document class, a cover letter and a submission manifest count here. Fixture: main.tex, where the repository markers are explicitly absent.

also_holds_with_note: Empty by contract, not by omission: also_holds_with joins schemas only (CONNECTION.md), and this is a template row. The co-activations this situation actually produces are already carried on the Research schema row — research also_holds_with college_applications (fixture Abstract_PVA-RDP_UChicago.pdf, recorded here as that example's also_schema) and research also_holds_with code (fixture main.tex under a repository marker).

falls_through_to.why: 00: "standalone certificates, notices, confirmations, forms, and PDFs that have a durable purpose but no broader group" — an acceptance letter, a signed licence agreement or a stranded proof whose project and venue never resolve. Fixtures: Signed_License_to_Publish_nmeth.pdf, Cover letter — Nature Methods.docx with no recoverable project.

00: "files whose meaning is partly understood but whose final location requires a future decision" — the sparse lifecycle files this situation produces in quantity: a response document with no project token, a marked-up proof scan, an unlabelled figure panel. Fixtures: Response to Reviewers.docx, Proof_marked_scan.pdf.

The collision with research.reading-library resolves here when the file is somebody else's paper: 00 defines the residual for exactly that — papers "that appear to be reading material but have no active research, course, or project association". Fixture: Ravikumar_2019_NatureMethods.pdf.

Submission and proof material arrives compressed and is sometimes password-protected, and 00 requires such an archive to be represented rather than forced: "Password-protected, malformed, nested, or oversized archives should be marked as unreadable or partially inspected rather than forced open". An unreadable submission_*.zip is represented, never guessed at from its name.

sensitivity_why: Not because publication is private, but because this situation holds unpublished manuscripts before they are public, confidential referee reports and editorial decision correspondence, and that correspondence arrives as mail, which 00 requires be handled "while treating addresses and message content as potentially sensitive". Referee anonymity is a second reason: a report's evidence must not be mined for an identity. The value is 00's phrase and nothing more; a handling class is P7's and none is assigned here.
open_question: Should venue be a folder level at all, or metadata only? This node recommends project → venue → stage because a rejected-then-resubmitted manuscript produces two complete submission families whose stage values otherwise interleave. But a researcher whose manuscripts each go to one journal gets a one-child level, which is precisely what 00 asks the canvas to warn about, and some people file by manuscript with the venue living in the filename instead. The fork decides a real folder structure and is Joseph's: does the recommendation lead with venue included and let the canvas offer flattening, or lead flat (project → stage) and offer venue as an optional split for multi-venue manuscripts?
